entry.title: Fuzzy String Matching in PostgreSQL with pg_trgm (Trigram Search Tutorial)
entry.summary:
🔍 Fuzzy String Matching in PostgreSQL with pg_trgm
When working with user data — names, addresses, search queries — exact string matching isn’t always enough. People make typos, use alternate spellings, or abbreviations. PostgreSQL provides a powerful extension called pg_trgm (trigram search) that allows you to perform fuzzy text matching and find “close enough” results. A trigram is simply a group of three consecutive characters from a string. For example, the word: Talemul
Would be split into trigrams (with start/end markers): " T", "Tal", "ale", "lem", "emu", "mul", "ul "
👉 Why the spaces? PostgreSQL pads the string at the beginning and end with spaces to catch edge cases.
